date_note: Star's article (published 26 November, 10:57) gives no earlier day for the detentions; the date is its publication day.
exec: Star reports Turkey's intelligence agency MİT disrupted a network that sought to infiltrate wireless networks of critical institutions, including defense industry firms.
geo_basis: country as stated by the source
plain: Star reports that Turkish intelligence says two people mapped Wi-Fi networks near sensitive sites in Ankara and Istanbul for a foreign intelligence service; both were jailed pending trial.
summary: Star reports that MİT and Istanbul Police detained two suspects accused of trying to infiltrate the wireless networks of critical institutions, including defense industry firms, in Ankara and Istanbul. According to the article, MİT's investigation found they acted on behalf of a foreign country's intelligence service, which it does not name. The article says they were recruited through social media job ads, were paid in cryptocurrency and were sent to prison pending trial.
title: Star: MİT detains two suspects accused of mapping Wi-Fi networks of critical institutions for a foreign intelligence service

validation.note: Only Star was read (page text partly garbled by encoding); MİT's own statement was not read.
